diagnostic_evidence.quote: then $p\mapsto\kappa_p$ displays a bifurcation of order $M$ at $p^\star$
Note that $M$ distinct eigenvalue trajectories must be present near an order-$M$ bifurcation, e.g., by the fundamental theorem of algebra.

issues.failure_explanation: A ramified eigenvalue of an analytically perturbed problem has a Puiseux series $\kappa_{p^\star}+\sum_{j\ge j_0}c_j(p-p^\star)^{j/M'}$ with $c_{j_0}\neq0$ for some $j_0\ge1$; the proof assumes without argument that the leading exponent is $1/M'$ ($j_0=1$). Via lem:bifurc_ord, the hypothesis $I(p)=(p-p^\star)^{1-1/M}\widetilde I(p)$ with $\widetilde I$ nonzero forces $\kappa_p'\sim(p-p^\star)^{-(1-1/M)}$, hence only $j_0/M'=1/M$: the leading Puiseux exponent is $1/M$ while the bifurcation order (number of coalescing branches, the paper's own notion) is $M'=j_0M$, an arbitrary multiple of $M$. The same unjustified $c_1\neq0$ assumption underlies the second characterization $I=(\kappa_p-\kappa_{p^\star})^{M-1}\overline I$ and the converse: for an order-$M$ branch with leading exponent $\ell_0/M$, $I$ vanishes like $(p-p^\star)^{1-\ell_0/M}$, so both factorizations with nonzero remainders hold iff $\ell_0=1$. Nothing in the source excludes $\ell_0\ge2$: a real one-sided branch $\kappa_{p^\star}+(p-p^\star)^{1/2}+(p-p^\star)^{3/4}$ would satisfy the hypotheses with $M=2$ while four branches coalesce.

failure_location.quote: Differentiating the above expression and enforcing the correct asymptotic order of $\kappa_p'$ as $p\to p^\star$ proves that $M'=M$, yielding the first claim.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem as the equivalence between "$I$ vanishes to one-sided exact order $1-1/M$" and "$\kappa_p-\kappa_{p^\star}$ has leading Puiseux term $c(p-p^\star)^{1/M}$, $c\neq0$, in lowest terms", concluding that the bifurcation order is a multiple of $M$; or add, and prove for the ITP, a genericity hypothesis that the first Puiseux coefficient of the cycle is nonzero (not established in the source).
issues.overall_effect: The exact-order guarantees of cor:bifurc_sufficient (both directions, both factorization criteria) are unsupported as written; the proof establishes only that the leading Puiseux exponent of $\kappa_p-\kappa_{p^\star}$ is $1/M$, i.e., that the bifurcation order is a multiple of $M$. prop:disk:bifurc invokes this for its cubic conclusion, but that conclusion is independently asserted by thm:old for the disk, so it is excluded from dependents; the annulus bifurcation criterion and the numerical order estimates use only zeros and the vanishing rate of $I$, which survive.
issues.title: Bifurcation order identified with the leading Puiseux exponent without justification
issues.why_classification: The source-supported repair weakens the advertised exact-order guarantee to a leading-exponent/order-divisibility statement: a limited weakening that preserves bifurcation detection and all applications (disk cubicity being independently covered by thm:old) without new global proof architecture; it exceeds minor because the theorem's conclusion itself changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: On the other hand, the indicator is strictly negative for real eigenvalue curves, except at bifurcation points, in agreement with \cref{cor:bifurc}.
Therein, we observe that the indicator becomes positive if and only if an eigenvalue trajectory is (i) real and (ii) traveling to the right.
although now all bifurcations are cubic and the indicator $\overline{I}$ is uniformly non-positive

issues.failure_explanation: In all reported tests $p>1$, so the factor $\frac{2}{a_m\pi(1-p^2)}$ in eq:ind_simpl is negative and $\overline I$ has the opposite sign of $I$. The paper's own disk identity (proof of prop:disk:bifurc) gives $\overline I(p)=|\alpha_p|^2J_m(\kappa_p)^2\ge0$ on real trajectories, with $\overline I(p)\sim+C|p-p^\star|^{2/3}$ at bifurcations; hence the reported "strictly negative" indicator, the fits "$\overline I(p)\sim-|p-p^\star|^\alpha$", and "the indicator $\overline I$ is uniformly non-positive" cannot describe the defined $\overline I$. Likewise, lem:bifurc_ord with $n_p=p^2$ gives $\operatorname{sign}\kappa_p'=\operatorname{sign}I(p)=-\operatorname{sign}\overline I(p)$ for $\kappa_p>0$, $p>1$, so "the indicator becomes positive iff the real trajectory is traveling to the right" (there attributed to cor:bifurc, though the sign relation comes from lem:bifurc_ord) holds for $I$, not for the defined $\overline I$. Every sign description is consistent with the plotted quantity being $I$ of eq:bifurc_indicator rather than $\overline I$ of eq:ind_simpl.

issues.overall_effect: The sign statements about the computed indicator in the disk and annulus numerical sections (text around fig:disk:ind, fig:disk:fit, fig:annulus:ind2zoom, fig:annulus:fit, and the disk/annulus comparison) contradict the paper's own definitions and lemmas, so the indicator plots cannot be reconciled with the theory as written. diagnostic_evidence.quote: a real (piecewise-smooth) eigenvalue trajectory undergoes bifurcation if and only if $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_1)}=r\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_r)}$

issues.failure_explanation: Writing $v_p(\rho,\theta)=f(\rho)\phi(m\theta)$ gives $\|v_p\|_{L^\infty(\partial B_\rho)}=|f(\rho)|$ but $\|v_p\|^2_{L^2(\partial B_\rho)}=\rho\,a_m\pi|f(\rho)|^2$, since the arclength measure on $\partial B_\rho$ is $\rho\,d\theta$. Hence the bifurcation condition $|f(1)|=r|f(r)|$ is equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\sqrt r\,\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$ (i.e., $\|v_p\|^2_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=r\|v_p\|^2_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$), not to equality of the two $L^2$ norms. For $0<r<1$ the stated equivalence is false whenever $f(r)\neq0$.

failure_location.quote: By the assumed polar-coordinate separability in \cref{eq:annulus:functions}, this is actually equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the claimed equality by $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\sqrt r\,\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$, or delete the sentence.
issues.overall_effect: A standalone incorrect restatement of the annulus bifurcation criterion; no other claim in the paper depends on it.
issues.title: False equivalence of the annulus bifurcation condition with boundary L2-norm equality
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction fixes the statement with no mathematical loss, and nothing else in the paper relies on the erroneous equivalence.
